title: Multi-Zone Landscape Post-Processing of a Winter Mountain Scene (ISO 3200)

date.basis: Embedded MP4 creation_time may reflect export date; no independent date confirmation in transcript.

summary: The video presents a step-by-step post-processing workflow for a winter mountain landscape captured at high ISO. The instructor identifies a flat lighting situation and a bright sky fragment that necessitates separate local adjustments, then outlines a multi-zone approach (sky, midground/mountain, and foreground) to achieve depth and atmosphere. The process moves from initial noise reduction and lighting adjustments to intricate color grading, tonal-based color adjustments, and non-destructive compositing between two Camera Raw instances. Techniques include isolating problematic zones, painting adjustments with a history-brush workflow, cloning and blending across states, and employing perspective and warp tools to guide the viewer’s eye toward the mountain peak. The tutor emphasizes precise tint handling, color calibration, texture management, and subtle diffusion to create a three-dimensional, dreamy winter scene while preserving snow texture and avoiding color artifacts.

sections.description: The speaker introduces a two-RAW workflow: reopen with adjustments intact, then replace problematic color using tonal-based edits to preserve luminance relationships and reduce color artifacts.
